Lithium explorer and developer Winsome Resources (ASX:WR1; “Winsome” or “the Company”) is pleased to announce the analysis of previously reported outcrop samples from its Sirmac-Clapier Project (Sirmac) in the Eeyou Istchee James Bay region of Quebec, Canada have confirmed the presence and tenor of very high grade cesium mineralisation. Exploration discovered a new, outcropping, high-grade spodumene-bearing pegmatite at Sirmac (refer ASX Announcement 10 February 2025). Assay results from systematic channel sampling identified the presence of high grade cesium mineralisation in addition to lithium mineralisation. Cesium assays previously reported were constrained by an upper detection limit of 25,000ppm Cs. Further analysis of selected samples which had originally assayed greater than 10,000ppm Cs has now been completed and has both confirmed the presence of very high grade cesium and provided more precise analyses of the cesium content of these samples as shown in Appendix 1. While the average cesium intersection across the outcrop has not increased significantly the more precise analysis has enabled two high cesium zones to be better delineated within Channel 2, with assays of 4m at 3.08% Cs20 + 1.27% Li.O and 4m at 2.23% Cs,0 + 2.13% Li;O (refer Table 1 below). The presence of very high grade cesium mineralisation is of interest given the scarcity of cesium across the world. Only 3 deposits have been mined to date, including the Sinclair Mine in Western Australia, and there are limited development projects globally. One of these is the Case Lake Project in northeastern Ontario owned by Power Metals Corp (TSX-V.PWM), with Winsome owning a 19.6% stake in Power Metals, valued at approximately A$35m, and the offtake rights to lithium, tantalum and cesium products. winsomeresources.com.au ASX:WR1 | FSE:4XJ | QTCQB:WRSLF  NN Er — mS g (i | NT — — —— N\ Ar ASX RELEASE ARC AMER EE ~WINSON ERERY RCES 20 February 2025 REN AN Addition of New Claims Following the identification of outcropping mineralisation at Sirmac a further 12 claims in the project area were added through low cost staking. This expands the landholding at Sirmac to 41.3km? (Figure 1) Sirmac is located 30km from provincial road infrastructure and also located 40km from the Moblan Lithium Deposit owned by Sayona (ASX.SYA). The regional centres of Chibougamau and Chapais, along with access to the rail network, are approximately 100km south of the project (Figure 3). Significantly, Sirmac is approximately 600km from the processing infrastructure at the Renard Operation by road. Winsome has an option over the Renard Operation as detailed in the ASX Announcements of 3 April 2024 and 4 December 2024.
